}).round(2)

# Check if there are upcoming peaks in Season 2 by looking at all days
trips = tables['trips']
s1_data = trips[trips['fish_date_season'] == 1].sort_values('fish_date_doy')
s2_data = trips[trips['fish_date_season'] == 2].sort_values('fish_date_doy')

print("Season 1: Days with >30 yt/trip average (strong fishing):")
s1_peaks = s1_data.groupby('fish_date_doy').agg({'yt': ['count', 'mean']})
s1_peaks.columns = ['trip_count', 'avg_yt']
s1_peaks = s1_peaks[s1_peaks['avg_yt'] >= 30].sort_values('avg_yt', ascending=False)
print(s1_peaks)

print("\n\nSeason 2 DOY > 270 (remaining season):")
s2_future = s2_data.groupby('fish_date_doy').agg({'yt': ['count', 'mean']})
s2_future.columns = ['trip_count', 'avg_yt']
s2_future = s2_future[s2_future.index > 270]
print(s2_future)
